Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina: okay team, thanks for carving time, uh, this is the pre-launch huddle for the inference GA. main objective is to trim scope to the minimum viable safe launch and make sure oncall knows what to do if latency spikes or multi-node oom happens.
[00:22] Marcus: yeah, agree. I'll start with the engineering constraints--we have two net blockers: sustained 95th p50 disparity on long-tail 8k prompts and the kv cache eviction spikes that popped in staging yesterday. Benji, can you summarize the perf findings?
[00:38] Benji: sure, um, so the 8k token batch workload shows a 1.6x token-per-second drop when we enable the new quant profile. it's probably noise, but there's also a kernel fallback we haven't fully instrumented. I flagged a possible NVLink contention in the perf sheet.
[00:58] Samir: just to interject, are we talking about the production quant profile or the experimental one? because we need to be careful exposing experimental quant to Hosted customers at GA.
[01:12] Benji: it's the q5b-experimental we ran last week; the recommended q4.1 profile looks more stable but cost is higher by ~12%.
[01:28] Rae: for SRE perspective, the bigger risk is that when KV cache eviction occurs under memory pressure, latency tails go through the roof and alerts cascade. yesterday the staging run caused two simultaneous paging events, and our paging alert group didn't fire fast enough because thresholds were set too conservative.
[01:50] Marcus: okay, so tangible asks: Benji to run an end-to-end pass with q4.1 + q5b in parallel with the longer seq distribution, produce a canary comparison. Rae to tighten the alerting. Tessa will coordinate scheduling.
[02:05] Tessa: yep. Also want to flag release window constraints—QA has a blackout the week of 12/8, so if we want ramping earlier we need to do a dry-run this week. can we commit to that?
[02:22] Lina: I want to make a call on scope now: streaming responses with function-calling and free-form tool invocation are nice-to-have for GA, but given the perf oscillation and oncall limited capacity, I'd like to scope streaming to beta and ship the non-streaming text/generation + embeddings first. Thoughts?
[02:45] Samir: i lean toward that. streaming adds more surface area for KV cache and persistent connection handling, plus more egress metrics. for initial users, request/response is fine.
[03:00] Benji: agree. shipping core generation + embeddings and deferring streaming reduces the kernel combos we need to test by maybe 30%.
[03:12] Marcus: ok that's a decision then. Lina, will you log that into the scope doc?
[03:19] Lina: yes, i'll update the scope doc after the call. i've added success criteria: error rate <0.5% p95 latency under expected traffic, and unit cost within 10% of projected.
[03:34] Rae: on the oncall side, couple of concrete items: 1) add an explicit fallback policy that routes to a lower-capacity model-variant when RT p95 breaches threshold for N minutes, 2) make the KV-cache eviction a P1 with a dedicated runbook, 3) lower the paging alert threshold from 85% to 78% for the first two weeks.
[03:58] Samir: the fallback routing: are we doing model-variant fallback in the control plane, or runtime-level auto-fallback? those are different complexity. If control-plane routing, we need a fast rollback path in the console.
[04:16] Benji: current plan was runtime auto-fallback because it's faster; we already have a circuit-breaker for model-serving but we need better observability to avoid cascading fallbacks. we don't want an auto-fallback that just thrashes between variants.
[04:34] Marcus: so action: Marcus and Benji to propose a fallback policy that includes cooldown and a manual override. add a dashboard for fallback count and recovery time.
[04:46] Rae: and we should include a SLO for fallback frequency in the canary gating. if fallback rate > X per minute then fail the canary.
[04:58] Tessa: i'll add that to the gating checklist. speaking of canary, what's the planned initial canary size?
[05:06] Lina: proposal is 1% of traffic for 24 hours with automatic rollback if error rate or fallback rate breaches. then expand to 5% for 48 hours with manual approval.
[05:18] Marcus: note that 1% might not surface rare long-tail prompts; we might need targeted traffic sampling from high-token customers. Benji, can we replay partner logs into canary?
[05:31] Benji: replay is possible but we need consent/PII scrubbed; the perf harness can run synthetic long-tail replays that approximate distribution.
[05:42] Samir: small interruption—do we have SOC2/audit requirements about logging for private deployments? some customers will want audit logs for every inference call. that impacts storage and cost assumptions.
[05:56] Lina: good point. we'll keep audit-log for private deployments as an opt-in enterprise feature; GA hosted will have aggregated logs and trace IDs but not raw payload retention by default. add to the security checklist.
[06:10] Rae: back to oncall: i want to run a tabletop this Friday with rotation leads. simulate a KV eviction cascade and practice failover. we should time the runbook actions.
[06:22] Tessa: friday works for me. i'll block 90 minutes for the dry-run with SRE and a couple of engineers from runtime.
[06:31] Benji: for the perf runs, i'll schedule an 8k token QPS sweep across q4.1/q5b and the fallback-enforced runtime tomorrow. results by Monday.
[06:41] Marcus: how are we instrumenting the kernel fallback path? last time logs were sparse.
[06:47] Benji: I've added extra tracing points but the exporter drop is still lossy at high throughput. i will instrument a dedicated path that writes to the perf store and not rely on the metrics-exporter aggregation.
[06:59] Rae: please make sure the exporter includes the instance id and a kv-cache eviction flag, so oncall can correlate.
[07:07] Samir: question about rollout comms—who owns customer comms if we need a partial rollback?
[07:12] Lina: product will own messaging; Tessa will coordinate the engineering rollback note. for enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private, CSMs will be looped in immediately.
[07:23] Tessa: I'll draft a short rollback/incident message template and share with CSMs.
[07:30] Marcus: one more technical detail: do we pin models by version for the canary, or allow runtime auto-upgrade? I prefer pinning for determinism.
[07:38] Benji: pinning the model version is safer. runtime auto-upgrade can be a later capability once we have stronger regression guards.
[07:44] Lina: agreed. pin model + quant profile for canary and GA.
[07:48] Rae: Ops question: what's the SLA target for the new feature at GA?
[07:52] Lina: target is 99.95% availability with p95 latency under X ms for baseline requests; exact numbers will be in the scope doc.
[07:59] Samir: small nit: we need to document per-route quotas and token caps for the initial rollout to avoid noisy tenants from skewing canary metrics.
[08:09] Marcus: noted. we'll enforce per-tenant token throttles in the gateway for the canary.
[08:16] Tessa: recap of decisions so far: defer streaming to beta, pin models/quant to stable profiles for canary, 1% then 5% canary expansion with explicit gating, oncall tabletop Friday, lower paging thresholds for the first two weeks. Lina will update scope doc and success criteria.
[08:38] Lina: thanks. any other concerns?
[08:42] Benji: just to surface cost: if we pin to q4.1, cost goes up ~12% but reduces risk. tradeoff needs signoff from finance for the GA forecast.
[08:53] Lina: i'll loop in finance inline and get a signoff.
[08:56] Rae: also, add a rollback checklist item to the runbook: steps to take when fallback doesn't recover in N minutes, include throttling and traffic redirection.
[09:05] Tessa: will do.
[09:07] Lina: ok, last thing—any blockers to do the dry-run this week?
[09:11] Marcus: no blockers from infra, we might need temporary quota bump for the replay. Benji will request it.
[09:17] Benji: requested.
[09:19] Lina: great. thanks everyone. i'll send updated scope by tomorrow EOD and include the success criteria and gating checklist.

Recap & Decisions (auto-generated/edited):
- Scope: GA = text generation + embeddings; streaming deferred to beta.
- Model/quant: pin to stable profiles (q4.1 recommended) for canary/GA; experimental q5b deferred.
- Canary: 1% for 24h (auto-rollback on gating breach) -> 5% for 48h manual approval.
- Oncall: tabletop Friday, lower paging thresholds, KV-cache eviction runbook P1, fallback policy with cooldown and manual override.
- Perf: Benji to do 8k token sweep and perf instrumentation; Marcus/Beni to design fallback dashboards.
